problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x)=2\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
worked_solution:
The zeros of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ are given by

$$
x=n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x)=2\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(2x-\frac{\pi }{6}).$ This gives

$$
2x-\frac{\pi }{6}=n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{\pi }{6} & =n\pi  \\ 2x & =n\pi +\frac{\pi }{6} \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x=\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.
